items.title: Retain valid review receipts across trusted closeout metadata writes
items.context: B-3aec proved that canonical test-evidence, done-required-evidence, live-smoke-transcript, summary, and delivery-check writes can invalidate already-valid review passes because latestValidCloseoutReceipt sees blank or non-canonical writer metadata. Introduce one shared closeout artifact writer and lineage contract and prove trusted metadata-only descendants preserve reviewer bindings while source or configuration drift still fails closed.

happy.desc: After a current signed reviewer pass, each registered closeout artifact writer records integrity-chained cooperative local-runtime lineage with a registered writer label; when only bounded story metadata intervenes, the existing reviewer receipt remains mechanically fresh, while specialized artifact gates independently validate schema, digest, reviewer, policy, command-set, and freshness facts. Hostile same-UID repository/runtime modification is an explicit non-goal unless a future isolated trust domain is configured.

A normal sequence containing several different registered closeout writers preserves the same review round and reviewer receipt across every intermediate HEAD, and the freshness result exposes an auditable trusted-metadata-descendant reason rather than silently weakening hash checks.

edge.desc: Repeated idempotent writes of the same canonical artifact and a trusted modify-then-revert metadata history remain retainable only when every intervening commit/path is classified by the shared canonical lineage evaluator.

Concurrent HEAD movement between lineage evaluation and artifact persistence is detected with a before/after HEAD check and refuses retention; a stable retry can then succeed without corrupting the prior receipt.
Legacy closeout evidence lacking the new writer envelope is handled by an explicit compatibility/refusal disposition and never implicitly promoted to trusted lineage.

The shared writer contract is consumed by every listed closeout artifact producer, and a consumer matrix proves every production gate uses its specialized validator rather than treating review-retention lineage as artifact approval.

adversarial.desc: Any source-code or story-owned material drift invalidates reviewer receipt retention even when surrounded by trusted metadata commits.
Configuration, validation policy, or validation command-set/order drift invalidates retention and reports the exact changed binding.
An unknown, misspelled, or non-registered writer label is rejected fail-closed inside the cooperative local-runtime boundary and cannot be laundered through a trusted metadata path.

Direct/manual artifact mutation without current coherent lineage invalidates retention even if content resembles a registered artifact; coherent hostile same-UID forgery remains an explicitly tested non-goal, not a claim of durable authority.
Malformed, unverifiable, non-ancestor, cyclic, or incoherent lineage data is rejected fail-closed with no reviewer-pass carry-forward.
A registered writer may not whitelist arbitrary dirty paths: user files, source, config, command entrypoints, and unregistered metadata remain untrusted.
Changing only headHash is insufficient for retention unless exact-head or fully verified trusted-metadata-descendant lineage plus unchanged material/storyFiles/policy/command-set bindings is proven.

items.title: Make REVIEW to TEST to DONE closeout ordering converge in one pass
items.context: REVIEW to TEST currently runs validate after review passes, then the new test evidence makes those passes stale. Delivery dispatch is TEST-only while delivery_check_set is REVIEW-capable, creating a circular ordering. Define and mechanically enforce a single legal order that produces validation, delivery, summary, live smoke, DONE-required evidence, reviewer receipts, and done_prepare report without DEV to REVIEW metadata-only round trips.

happy.desc: Starting with one current complete REVIEW round, the standard unattended REVIEW→TEST→DONE path produces routine validation evidence, delivery check, summary, live-smoke transcript, DONE-required evidence, and a PASS done_prepare report, then reaches DONE with zero metadata-only DEV/REVIEW backsteps, zero extra reviewer re-attestations, zero human confirmations, and zero re-execution of an unchanged validation command set.

Machine-readable closeout telemetry proves one-pass convergence by reporting the initial/final phase, review round and receipt identity, artifact write sequence, validation disposition/commandExecutions, re-attestation count, human-ack count, and rollback reasons; the successful fixture asserts rollback=0, reAttestation=0, humanAck=0, unchangedSuiteExecutions=0.

edge.desc: Delivery reviewer dispatch and delivery_check_set have the same mechanically enforced legal phase/cardinality; dispatching and writing in that phase succeeds, while the prompt never instructs an action the handler rejects.

A fresh unchanged routine validation or DONE-required receipt is reused through the canonical evaluator and records disposition=reused with commandExecutions=0; an explicit validate:false remains a distinct skipped/not-run state and cannot masquerade as reuse or PASS.

Each trusted closeout write performed after review preserves the current reviewer receipt through canonical lineage, including multiple metadata commits and an immediate idempotent done_prepare retry.
A closeout retry after a classified infrastructure interruption resumes from durable fresh artifacts without duplicating reviewer work, human acknowledgement, or unchanged commands.

The ordered closeout transaction remains deterministic when optional live-smoke or DONE-required policy is disabled: omitted phases are explicitly not-applicable and budgets/counts include only enabled phases.

adversarial.desc: Delivery dispatch outside its declared legal phase and delivery_check_set outside that same phase are both rejected before mutation with aligned diagnostics; no REVIEW-capable writer/TEST-only dispatcher mismatch remains.

A true source, story-owned, config, policy, or command-set drift during closeout refuses reuse and requires the appropriate validation/review action; one-pass optimization never carries stale assurance across real material change.

A validation command that genuinely fails remains a validation failure and follows the documented lifecycle response; metadata-loop prevention cannot convert it to infra failure, advisory, reuse, or PASS.

Unknown writer, manual tamper, malformed/unsigned lineage, or concurrent HEAD change stops closeout fail-closed without fabricating reviewer re-attestation or silently asking a human to acknowledge convergence.

The closeout orchestrator cannot invoke validation twice through nested REVIEW→TEST advance plus done_prepare; a command spy asserts each changed suite executes at most once and an unchanged suite executes zero times.

Writing summary, transcript, delivery, validation, or DONE-required artifacts in any permutation not admitted by the canonical ordering cannot invalidate receipts and then silently bounce to DEV/REVIEW; it must either be normalized by the shared writer or rejected with a bounded next action.

No convergence breaker/human-ack path is entered solely because trusted closeout metadata advanced HEAD; a test fails if any human:true resume/ack command is requested in the positive closeout transcript.

items.title: Eliminate concept deleted-symbol false positives for body-only edits
items.context: Concept preflight reported buildQueryGroups, candidateReadBindingErrors, and defaultHostRunRunner as deleted even though exports and consumers remained. Bind deletion detection to declaration identity or signature disappearance rather than semantic-anchor body changes, while retaining true deletion and residual-reference blocking.

happy.desc: Editing only the body of an existing exported function while preserving its declaration identity/signature is classified as modified, not deleted; concept preflight does not emit a deleted-symbol blocker for buildQueryGroups, candidateReadBindingErrors, defaultHostRunRunner, or equivalent declarations.

Removing a declaration (or changing it so its prior declaration identity/signature truly disappears) is classified as a true deletion, and remaining imports/calls/references produce the existing residual-reference blocker.

edge.desc: Body-only edits that add/remove nested control-flow blocks, local variables, callbacks, object properties, or semantic anchors do not affect the enclosing declaration identity.

Whitespace, comments, formatting, generic/type annotation changes that preserve the configured signature identity, and moving a declaration within the same file follow an explicit stable classification rather than regex-anchor disappearance.

Supported declaration forms—exported/non-exported function declarations, const/arrow functions, async/generator functions, class methods, constructors, and overload declarations—are matched by syntax-aware declaration identity with deterministic handling of duplicate names/scopes.
A deliberate rename is represented as old-symbol deletion plus new-symbol addition (or an explicit rename relation) and still checks residual references to the old declaration.

adversarial.desc: An identifier with the deleted symbol name appearing only in comments, strings, nested locals, object keys, or an unrelated scope cannot satisfy declaration-presence or suppress a true deletion.

A declaration retained but made unreachable, unexported, or signature-incompatible is not blindly accepted as body-only; the classifier reports the actual identity/export/signature change and applies the appropriate blocker.
Deleting one of multiple same-name declarations or overloads is detected by file/scope/kind/signature identity rather than hidden by another declaration with the same text name.

Parser failure, malformed source, unsupported syntax, or ambiguous declaration identity fails closed with a typed diagnostic; it must not silently report no deletion or fall back to the old semantic-anchor false-positive regex.

The regression corpus contains paired fixtures for body-only modification versus true declaration deletion using the three symbols observed in B-3aec, and asserts both no false positive and no false negative/residual-reference regression.

items.userSees: User sees "no deleted exports" for declaration/body edits, while a true deletion with residual references remains WARN or FAIL.
